scope: One bounded official-kernel (fla-core 0.5.2 chunk_gated_delta_rule) numerical and performance probe on one drained GPU. Reference process runs the current pure-Torch fallback with fla absent; candidate process resolves the official FLA function via the transformers use_kernel_func_from_hub_with_fallback mechanism. 0 formal training updates, 0 navigation episodes, probe optimizer updates discarded.

chunks: longest_stop: same record, terminal STOP step
mid_a: first distinct record with decisions>=12, steps 4-7
fixed_decision_set.timing_block: short record, min(16,len) decisions, 1 warmup + 1 measured pass, forward+backward, no optimizer step
fixed_decision_set.loss: unweighted 4-class CE summed over the fixed set (matches v6 unweighted_action_ce)
fixed_decision_set.optimizer: AdamW lr=1e-4 wd=0.01 betas=(0.9,0.999) eps=1e-8, clip=1.0, exactly 1 diagnostic update per process, discarded

thresholds.rationale: BF16 reduction-order tolerance; q/k are l2-normalized before FP32 in the fallback so small absolute differences are expected. update_relative_l2 reuses the D1 gate value 0.15. No threshold is relaxed after observation; FAIL stays FAIL.

determinism: torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) in both processes, matching current training. If the official kernel cannot execute under deterministic mode the probe records FAIL instead of flipping the flag.
causal_conv1d: stays pure-Torch fallback in both modes (causal_conv1d package not acquired); identical across modes
output: kernel_probe_v1/run_v1/ (LEASE_BEFORE, LEASE_ACTIVE, drain jsonl, PROBE_REFERENCE/CANDIDATE .pt+.json, RESTORATION, LEASE_RESULT, COMPARISON)
not_authorized_here: formal training, navigation episodes, multi-GPU, any production queue or GPU0/1/2/6/7 process, environment mutation
